roles.name: Pigeon
roles.text: Visit a player and lay an egg in their nest.

roles.name: Lazy Pigeon
roles.text: Visit a player and lay an egg in the nest of the player they visited (if any). You see yourself as a Pigeon, but other players see you as a Lazy Pigeon.

roles.name: Hawk
roles.text: Visit a player. If they are Meowfia, lay an egg in your nest.

roles.name: Blind Hawk
roles.text: Visit a player. If the player they visited is Meowfia, lay an egg in your nest.

roles.name: Black Swan
roles.text: Visit yourself every night and learn your role. If you are still Black Swan, lay an egg in your nest.

roles.name: Ugly Duckling
roles.text: You appear as Meowfia to investigators. Visit a player and steal all eggs from their nest.
roles.reading: "All eggs from their nest" is every card in the victim's hand at nightfall, up to the nightly cap of 5. The victim discards; the Duckling draws the same number.

roles.name: Kookaburra
roles.text: Visit a player. Learn their role. If anyone visits you, you will be confused.
roles.reading: A confused Kookaburra learns a wrong animal.

roles.name: Tit
roles.text: Visit a player and choose a role. If they are that role, lay an egg in your nest.

roles.name: Eagle
roles.text: Visit a player and learn which players visited them. Lay an egg in your nest for every visitor they had.

roles.name: Falcon
roles.text: Visit a player and learn who they visited. If they visited no one, lay an egg in your nest.

roles.name: Pelican
roles.text: Visit a player. All players that visit you visit that player instead. Lay an egg for every redirected visitor.

roles.name: Turkey
roles.text: Stay home. Lay an egg in the nest of each player who visits you.

roles.name: Owl
roles.text: Visit a player. You will learn of all the animals (not players) that visited them at night. If no one visited them (apart from you), lay an egg in their nest.

roles.name: Mosquito
roles.text: You will visit a random player at night, lay an egg in their nest, and confuse them.
roles.reading: The app picks the target at random.

roles.name: Seagull
roles.text: Visit a player. They swap nests with the player they visited (if any). If both nests had the same number of eggs, lay an egg in your nest.
roles.reading: The two players swap whole hands at dawn, before eggs are drawn or discarded.

roles.name: Goose
roles.text: In a round where a player is the Goose, winners are losers and losers are winners during scoring (each Goose inverts it once, so two Geese cancel out). Visit a player: lay an egg in their nest and both their neighbours' nests.

roles.name: Chicken
roles.text: Visit a player and lay an egg in their nest. If anyone throws a single egg at you during eggsecution, you lose (even if Farm wins).
roles.reading: The Chicken loses if anyone throws any card at it.

roles.name: Crane
roles.text: Choose an animal from the pool. If that animal is in play, visit that player and lay an egg in their nest. If not, lay an egg in your nest.

roles.name: Cuckoo
roles.text: You are secretly the Cuckoo, but you believe you are another animal. You will perform that animal's night actions, but none of it actually happens. Instead, you visit yourself and lay an egg in your nest. Other players will see you as the Cuckoo.
roles.reading: Believes they are a random Farm animal from the pool. Their choices do nothing.

roles.name: Emu
roles.text: You see yourself as Emu, but you are actually an unused farm role from the pool (or Pigeon if there are none left). Choose someone to visit at night; you will do your actual role's action on them (if any). Other players see your real role.
roles.reading: The hidden animal is a random Farm animal in the pool that nobody was dealt (else Pigeon).

roles.name: Crow
roles.text: You will visit a random Meowfia player and lay an egg in their nest (without knowing who they are).

roles.name: Magpie
roles.text: You will learn of an animal at night. Three random players will each receive an egg in their nest; one of them is the animal you learned about.

roles.name: Galah
roles.text: Visit a player and sing a song of three animals to them. One random player will receive an egg in their nest, and that player is one of the three animals you sang about.
roles.reading: The visited player hears the three animals; the Galah learns them too.

roles.name: Rainbow Lorikeet
roles.text: Each player that visits you receives a Wink. Visit a player. If they have a Wink, lay an egg in your nest.
roles.reading: A wink kills at once during the day; nobody is told who winked.

roles.name: Lovebird
roles.text: Visit a player. If they are the same alignment as the player they visited, lay an egg in your nest.

roles.name: Lyrebird
roles.text: Visit a player. Lay eggs in your nest equal to their egg count.
roles.reading: "Their egg count" is the number of cards in their hand at nightfall, up to the nightly cap of 5.

roles.name: Dove
roles.text: Visit a player and cure any status effects they have. Then, lay eggs in your nest for every remaining status effect active on any player (e.g. hugged, confused).

roles.name: Peacock
roles.text: At the start of the night, players will learn that you are the Peacock. Visit a player and lay two eggs.
roles.reading: Announced to the whole table as night falls.

roles.name: Cassowary
roles.text: Visit a player at night. If they have any eggs in their nest, kill them.
roles.reading: "Any eggs in their nest" is any card in hand, so the visit kills unless the Cassowary is hugged or the target's hand is empty.

roles.name: Fairy Penguin
roles.text: Visit a player and hug them. Lay an egg in your nest for every status effect active (e.g. hugged, confused).

roles.name: Vogelkop
roles.text: Visit a player and confuse them. Lay eggs in your nest for every Meowfia-aligned player in play.

roles.name: Sheep
roles.text: Visit a player. You are now their alignment.

roles.name: Frog
roles.text: Visit a player and swap animals with them. You will learn your new animal.
roles.reading: Each alignment moves with its animal, so a Frog that swaps with a cat becomes Meowfia.

roles.name: Switcheroo
roles.text: Visit a player. They will swap animals with the player they visited.
roles.reading: Each alignment moves with its animal.

roles.name: Koala
roles.text: Visit a player. You will confuse them. Any players that visit you will become confused.

roles.name: Clownfish
roles.text: Visit a player and do nothing. If you are eggsecuted, you win all the eggs thrown at you.

roles.name: Brumby
roles.text: Visit a player. Roles will rotate clockwise equal to the number of eggs in their nest.
roles.reading: The number of seats is the cards in the visited player's hand. Each alignment moves with its animal.

roles.name: Sheepdog
roles.text: Visit a player and hug them. If there are any Sheep in the game, you will learn who they are.

roles.name: Rabbit
roles.text: In games with a Rabbit, another player will also start as a Rabbit. Rabbits wake up together.
roles.reading: The second Rabbit is a random other player, who keeps their own alignment.

roles.name: Wasp
roles.text: Start with a Wink. You must use it before the round ends or you specifically will lose, regardless of your team's outcome.

roles.name: Gecko
roles.text: Choose a player at night. You immediately become a copy of their role and perform their action.
roles.reading: Chooses two players: whose animal to copy, then who to use the copied ability on. Keeps its own alignment. Copying a redirecting or two-player animal has no further effect.

roles.name: Quokka
roles.text: Visit a player and give them a Wink. If you die during the round, gain a bonus 3 eggs to your hand at the end of the round.

roles.name: Spider
roles.text: Visit a player. Anyone who visits that player will visit the player they visited instead, and vice versa.

roles.name: House Cat
roles.text: Visit a player. Learn their role and who they visited.

roles.name: Mouser
roles.text: Start with a Wink. Visit a player and learn their role.

roles.name: Sphinx
roles.text: You will learn all of the farm roles in play. Choose a role: you will visit a player who is that role and learn who they are.

roles.name: Floofer
roles.text: Visit a player and hug them. Any players that visit you will be hugged.

roles.name: Cat Burgler
roles.text: Visit a player and steal up to 3 eggs from their nest. Choose another player to give any number of the stolen eggs to.
roles.reading: Steals up to 3 cards' worth: the victim discards, and the Burgler and the chosen player draw.

roles.name: Maine Coon
roles.text: Visit a player. During the day, at any point before voting, you may stand up, bet any number of cards from your nest, and guess each player's animal. If you are correct, you win exclusively. Otherwise, you lose exclusively.
roles.reading: Guess every other player's animal on a day turn. Right: the round ends and only the Maine Coon scores (the bet is banked). Wrong: they die and lose the bet and the round.

roles.name: Top Cat
roles.text: Visit a player. They will switch alignments. If you switched a Meowfia to Farm, steal one of their eggs.
roles.reading: When it turns a Meowfia player Farm, that player discards a card and the Top Cat draws one.

roles.name: Rag Doll
roles.text: Visit a player and choose another player. The player you visited will instead visit the chosen player. Learn who every player visited at night.

roles.name: Copycat
roles.text: Choose a player. You will immediately become a copy of their animal (but keep your Meowfia alignment) and perform their action.
roles.reading: Chooses two players: whose animal to copy, then who to use the copied ability on. Copying a redirecting or two-player animal has no further effect.

flowers.name: Sunflower
flowers.text: At any point during the day, a player can spend one egg from their hand to secretly learn if a chosen player is a certain animal or not. Discard this card afterwards.

flowers.name: Bookworm
flowers.text: Farm players are given an identical secret word at night, Meowfia players a different one. At the end of the day, the eggsecuted player may guess both words; a correct guess makes that team win instead.

flowers.name: Pitcher Plant
flowers.text: At the start of the day, the app announces who visited whom (but not their roles or what happened during the visit).

flowers.name: Cactus Flower
flowers.text: At the start of the day, the app reveals exactly how many Meowfia there are. If there are zero, the round is skipped: no discussion, no vote, no eggs lost. Everyone scores +1 per egg in hand.
flowers.reading: The skipped round's bonus is on top of the 1 point each kept card is worth at the end.

flowers.name: Lotus
flowers.text: The 3 new pool cards are added face-down. Players do not know what was added; roles are still assigned from the full pool. The hidden cards are revealed after scoring.
flowers.note: Not simulated: nothing is added to the pool during a game here.

flowers.name: Corpse Flower
flowers.text: The eggsecuted player's role and alignment are not revealed, nobody learns which team won, and scoring for this round stays hidden until the end of the game.
flowers.note: No consolation card is returned this round (it would reveal the result).
flowers.reading: No consolation card is returned this round, since it would reveal the result.

flowers.name: Banksia
flowers.text: Players cannot talk normally this round. Communication is limited to whispering to the player sitting next to you. Players may freely make bird sounds or meow.
flowers.note: Public speech is limited to animal noises; whispers go only to a neighbour.
flowers.reading: Only animal noises aloud; whispers go to a neighbour.

flowers.name: Flannel Flower
flowers.text: Players must keep their eyes shut during the entire day phase. Discussion continues normally; you just can't see anyone.
flowers.note: Speech in the town square is shown without speaker names.
flowers.reading: Speech is shown without the speaker's name.

flowers.name: Marigold
flowers.text: Discussion is replaced by structured speeches: from the dealer clockwise, each player pleads their case while nobody else speaks. Then a short open discussion before voting.

flowers.name: Tumbleweed
flowers.text: Players walk freely around the room while discussing, forming clusters and whispering to anyone.
flowers.note: Players may whisper to anyone as well as speak publicly.

flowers.name: Bluebell
flowers.text: At any point during the day, a single player may say "CAW CAW" to gain one egg and immediately end the day. Discard this card afterwards.

flowers.name: Nightshade
flowers.text: For the next round, there will be a Dusk phase before the Night phase, where players talk openly and discuss their plans for the night.

flowers.name: Mulberry
flowers.text: The day starts short. Whenever it runs out, any player may spend one egg to extend it; if nobody pays, voting begins.
flowers.note: Each extension is one more beat of discussion.
flowers.reading: Each extension is one more beat of discussion; players are asked after every beat.

flowers.name: Stinging Bush
flowers.text: During the day, the first player to touch another player assassinates them. That player dies and cannot take part in the vote. Discard this card afterwards.
flowers.note: A player "touches" someone with a special action.

flowers.name: Moonflower
flowers.text: Two Night phases before Dawn: everyone acts twice. Dawn reports combine both nights and the nest egg cap of 5 is removed.

flowers.name: Wolfsbane
flowers.text: The chance of being Meowfia is 1 in 2 instead of 1 in 3. The app announces it before roles are assigned.

flowers.name: Twinflower
flowers.text: No limit on how many players can share the same role.

flowers.name: Angel's Trumpet
flowers.text: Laying and stealing eggs between players is inverted: laying in another nest steals from it instead, and stealing from another nest lays in it instead. Self-directed egg actions are unaffected.

flowers.name: Dandelion
flowers.text: Night actions resolve in seating order from the dealer instead of the normal resolution order.

flowers.name: Wildflower
flowers.text: A strange random event happens during the night.

flowers.name: Chocolate Lily
flowers.text: Hand sizes are hidden this round, and players may lie about them.

flowers.name: Foxglove
flowers.text: During the day, players may openly trade cards from their hands.

flowers.name: Bottlebrush
flowers.text: Players may throw eggs at this flower. If it receives the most eggs, nobody is eliminated and the round plays another night and day. Eggs thrown at the flower are lost.
flowers.reading: If it gets the most eggs, those eggs are lost, other thrown cards go back to their nests, and the round plays another night and day.

flowers.name: Tigerlily
flowers.text: Players place eggs in front of suspects during the day while players randomly die.

flowers.name: Snapdragon
flowers.text: Eggsecution is an open clockwise auction instead of a simultaneous vote.

flowers.name: Poppy
flowers.text: You choose how many eggs to throw, but they are drawn at random from your shuffled hand.

flowers.name: Venus Flytrap
flowers.text: The two players who receive the most eggs are both eggsecuted. Each elimination is scored independently; eggs thrown at a player who was not eliminated score nothing.
flowers.reading: Eggs thrown at a player who was not eliminated are discarded.

flowers.name: Wax Flower
flowers.text: You win if you threw eggs at any player on the opposite team, regardless of who was eggsecuted; you lose if you threw only at your own team.

flowers.name: Crimson Kunzea
flowers.text: Before you have spoken during the day, you may double down: throw your eggs at a player there and then, for all to see. That is your vote, and your score for this round is doubled.
flowers.note: Doubling adds the value you bank this round again as bonus points. The eggs you throw as you double down leave your nest at once; you do not throw again at the eggsecution.
flowers.reading: Doubling adds the value banked this round again as bonus points.

flowers.name: Oleander
flowers.text: Kept eggs are worth 0 points instead of 1 this round.
flowers.note: Not simulated: scoring counts kept cards only at the end of the game.

flowers.name: Thistle
flowers.text: The current scoreboard is announced. The last-place player becomes the Grudge Player: their thrown eggs count double as votes and score double if their team wins.

flowers.name: Golden Wattle
flowers.text: Two players may shake hands to bond. At the end of the round, bonded players of the same alignment each get +3 points; if different, the Farm player gets -3 and the Meowfia player +3.
flowers.note: A player offered a handshake must accept or decline it at once.
flowers.reading: A player offered a handshake must accept or decline it at once.

flowers.name: Desert Pea
flowers.text: During the day, a player may bet eggs and guess every player's animal. If correct, they are the sole winner of the round; if not, they are killed and lose their bet. Discard this card afterwards.

flowers.name: Waratah
flowers.text: Next round, players draft an animal from their hand to be their role.

flowers.name: Amaranth
flowers.text: After the first eggsecution, a second night, day and eggsecution is played.

flowers.name: Bird of Paradise
flowers.text: An extra bot player joins the round.

groups.label: Who is Meowfia
groups.help: How many players are Meowfia each round, and how animals are dealt.

groups.label: Cards and the pool
groups.help: Nest sizes, the deck and what is revealed each round.

groups.label: Dusk
groups.help: Talk before the night, about plans for the night.

groups.label: Dawn reports
groups.help: What players are told in the morning.

groups.label: Day discussion
groups.help: How the table talks, and what it is shown.

groups.label: Scoring
groups.help: What cards are worth and what happens to them.

groups.label: Single animals
groups.help: Fixes to one animal or to Winks. The card's text changes with the setting.

groups.label: Rules text
groups.help: What the players are told, without changing how the game plays.

settings.label: How many Meowfia
settings.help: By table size: 1 at four players, 1 or 2 at five or six, 2 or 3 at seven or eight; which it is each round is not announced. Or every player rolls the chance below.

settings.label: Chance of being Meowfia
settings.help: Each player rolls separately, every round. Only used when players roll a chance.

settings.label: Set number of Meowfia: fewest
settings.help: Only used when the most is above 0. Set both to the same number for exactly that many.

settings.label: Set number of Meowfia: most
settings.help: Above 0, a set number of players are Meowfia each round, between the fewest and the most, whatever is chosen above. 0 means use the choice above.

settings.label: Most Meowfia in a round
settings.help: Extra Meowfia rolls become Farm.

settings.label: One player per animal
settings.help: Each animal goes to at most one player; extra players get the Pigeon or the House Cat.

settings.label: Starting nest
settings.help: Cards dealt to each player before round 1.

settings.label: Cards drawn each round
settings.help: Cards every player draws at the start of each round.

settings.label: Flowers in play
settings.help: This many of the chosen flowers are picked at random when the game starts. They stay in play for the whole game, except one whose card says to discard it after use. 0 means no flowers.

settings.label: At most one self-deceiving animal
settings.help: Experiment (report 6.8): at most one of the Lazy Pigeon, Cuckoo and Emu is in the pool, and the rules say so.

settings.label: Meowfia see each other
settings.help: Experiment (report 6.4): at the start of each round the Meowfia are told who the others are, and each is shown a Farm animal not in play (a lone cat two). Animals that change a side overnight are left out of the pool.

settings.label: Pool size
settings.help: Experiment (report 6.8): the pool holds Farm animals equal to the Farm players plus three, chosen at random from those switched on.

settings.label: Announce scores each round
settings.help: At the start of every round after the first the Storyteller lists everyone's score. Off: score piles stay secret until the end (report 6.7).

settings.label: Show animals after each round
settings.help: When a round ends, everyone's animal, side and score are shown to the table. Off: only the eggsecuted player's side is known. A Corpse Flower round stays hidden.

settings.label: Wild cards in the deck
settings.help: Wilds are worth 0.

settings.label: Turns of talk before the night
settings.help: A Dusk phase every round, after the deal: players can only speak. 0 means no Dusk (the Nightshade still gives one).

settings.label: Most eggs a nest can change by
settings.help: Per night. The Moonflower lifts it.

settings.label: "Eggs in their nest" means
settings.help: For the Ugly Duckling, Lyrebird, Cassowary and Brumby.

settings.label: Confusion gives wrong animals
settings.help: A confused player who learns an animal is told a wrong one.

settings.label: Confusion changes the nest
settings.help: A confused player draws or discards by the wrong number. Off: only the report is wrong.

settings.label: Dawn report shows
settings.help: What a player is told when eggs were both laid and taken.

settings.label: Egg tokens
settings.help: Experiment (report 6.6): eggs laid or taken at night are public tokens, counted from zero each round, and become cards drawn or discarded only after the vote; confusion changes what a player is told, never their tokens.

settings.label: Tell hugged players
settings.help: Experiment (report 6.8): a hugged player's dawn report says their animal did nothing.

settings.label: Tell players they were confused
settings.help: Shown on their dawn report.

settings.label: Tell players their new animal or side
settings.help: When a swap changed it during the night.

settings.label: How the table talks
settings.help: Turns: The day is a set number of beats. In each, every player gets one turn, a few players at a time. Live: A conversation on a clock. After every message each player writes a short next line and bids 0 to 3 for the floor; the highest bidder speaks, and a player who was just named gets +1. Speaking to one player starts a back-and-forth between the two. CAW CAW counts without the floor. Messages arrive one at a time with pauses, and a browser player can speak whenever they like. Costs one Claude turn per player for every message outside an exchange.

options.label: Turns: everyone speaks once per beat
Live: players bid to speak, no turn order

settings.label: Turns of discussion
settings.help: Turns only. Everyone gets one turn to speak in each.

settings.label: Groups per turn
settings.help: Turns only. Players in a group speak at once; later groups have heard earlier ones. More groups means more back-and-forth and a slower game.

settings.label: Live talk: words of talk per player
settings.help: The length of the day. Every word spoken runs the clock down; 150 words is about a minute of speech.

settings.label: Live talk: word limit per message
settings.help: Short messages make a conversation of questions and answers; long ones make speeches.

settings.label: Live talk: replies each in an exchange
settings.help: When a player speaks to one other, the two talk back and forth this many times each before the floor reopens. 0 means no exchanges.

settings.label: Live talk: CAW CAW opens after
settings.help: The share of the clock that must run before CAW CAW can be called, so a day cannot end before anyone has been questioned.

settings.label: Live talk: pauses
settings.help: How long a message holds the floor before the next one appears. 1 is natural, 0 is no pauses, 2 is slow.

settings.label: When you play: seconds to read a message
settings.help: The pause after a 25-word message from another player. Shorter messages wait less and longer ones more. Only when a person plays in the browser. 0 is no pause.

settings.label: Word limit per turn
settings.help: How much a player may say at once.

settings.label: CAW CAWs to end the day
settings.help: How many different players must call it.

settings.label: CAW CAW waits for everyone
settings.help: Experiment (report 6.8): CAW CAW counts only once every living player has spoken.

settings.label: Allow whispers
settings.help: Private messages between two players during the day.

settings.label: Show egg counts during the day
settings.help: Every nest size is announced at the start of the day, as at a real table. Off: nobody sees how many eggs anyone else holds.

settings.label: What a vote is
settings.help: Experiment (report 6.1): one vote per living player, with the cards thrown only a stake. Standard: every card thrown is one vote.

settings.label: How the vote is taken
settings.help: Experiment (report 6.5): when the day ends everyone points at one player; the two with the most fingers are on trial and each answers once; then everyone votes and stakes between those two. Standard: one secret vote at anyone.

settings.label: Most cards you can throw
settings.help: 0 means no limit.

settings.label: Allow a throw at Nobody
settings.help: A bet that there are no Meowfia. It banks if right; if Nobody gets the most votes, no one is eggsecuted.

settings.label: A tied vote
settings.help: Who goes out when the most-egged players are level.

options.label: A Farm player goes out (ties favour Meowfia)

settings.label: Team mode
settings.help: Experiment (report 6.7): each player on the side that wins a round scores one point and thrown cards go back to their nests, so eggs are evidence and votes only. Standard: points.

settings.label: What a stake pays on
settings.help: Experiment (report 6.2): a Farm stake banks if its target is Meowfia, whoever goes out; a Meowfia stake banks (at the multiple below) if its target is the Farm player eggsecuted; everyone on the winning side also scores the side bonus. Standard: your side winning the round.

settings.label: Side bonus
settings.help: With stakes paid on your own read: points for everyone on the winning side.

settings.label: Meowfia stake multiple
settings.help: With stakes paid on your own read: a Meowfia stake that lands banks this many times its value.

settings.label: Points per card kept
settings.help: For each card still in your nest when the game ends.

settings.label: Consolation card
settings.help: On the losing side but threw at the other team: your best thrown card comes back.

settings.label: Banked cards
settings.help: Returning them keeps the deck from running out.

options.label: Are recorded, then return to the discard pile

settings.label: Nest limit after scoring
settings.help: 0 means no limit. Lowest cards are discarded first.

settings.label: House Cat leaves an egg
settings.help: It lays an egg in the nest it visits, so a cat can claim to be a Pigeon and the counts agree.

settings.label: The Top Cat
settings.help: Swapping keeps the number of Meowfia the same.

options.label: Flips its target to the other side

settings.label: Maine Coon must challenge early
settings.help: No challenge once anyone has called CAW CAW.

settings.label: Eggs for a Wink that hits the other side
settings.help: 0 means none.

settings.label: Extra clarifications
settings.help: Adds three reminders to the rules (a dead player can be eggsecuted; the setup draw is not evidence; sides are dealt afresh every round) and spells out the Pelican.

settings.label: Remind the table of the Goose
settings.help: At the vote, when it inverts the scoring.

testing.label: Testing setup
testing.help: No flowers and a fixed pool of simple animals, so every player has a different one.

control.label: Control
control.help: The frozen control for experiments: the basics pool at the standard rules of 13 November 2026.
